newsitem.title: UK: Turkey mandates bond despite likely early election.
newsitem.headline: Turkey mandates bond despite likely early election.

text.p: Turkey awarded the mandate for an imminent jumbo mark Eurobond on Monday, despite the possibility of an early election.
Analysts said an election would be positive for Turkey and investors were taking the announcement in their stride with political risks in Turkey already discounted.
"There's always a level of uncertainty with Turkey," Chase Manhattan London research head Robin Hubbard said.
"Any political uncertainty will make investors more cautious, but that does not mean there will be a big market reaction because the bonds are very tightly held."
Hubbard said any new issues would likely be launched at a wider spread.
Turkey announced the mandate for a one billion mark, five-year Eurobond to be jointly lead-managed by Commerzbank and West Deutsche Landesbank.
Over the weekend, Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan called for snap elections to resolve a row between his Islamist-led coalition and Turkey's secularist generals.
No date was set for polling.
"We hope elections will produce a more stable government," BankAmerica emerging markets economist Richard Gray said.

"There are all sorts of possible political permutations in Turkey and generally the markets don't like political uncertainty, but almost all permutations are better than what we have at the moment," he added.

Meanwhile state minister Ufuk Soylemez said the launch of the upcoming 1.0 billion mark five-year Eurobond would bring the country's total Eurobond issues for the first six months of this year to $1.35 billion.
"This total is more than half of the $2 billion foreign borrowing planned for this year," he said.
Turkish launched a $400 million five-year Eurobond in mid-May to yield 350 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. It had last tightened to trade around 288 b.p. over, dealers said.
The bond pays a psychologically attractive coupon of 10.0 percent.
In January, Turkey launched a seven-year 500 million mark bond via Commerzbank and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The bond was priced to yield 275 b.p. over the November 2003 Treuhand and was last trading at 200 b.p over, dealers said.
The bond pays a coupon of 7.75 percent.
Turkey is rated B1 by Moody's Investors Service and B by Standard & Poor's.
